title: Gold at Rs 1,43,873 and Silver at Rs 1,92,075 on October 30 Ahead of Dhanteras
excerpt: 24K gold eased to Rs 1,43,873 per 10 grams and 999 silver to Rs 1,92,075 per kg on October 30, a week before Dhanteras on November 6 and Diwali on November 8.
body:
• On October 30, 24K gold was priced at Rs 1,43,873 per 10 grams and 22K at Rs 1,31,788 per 10 grams on the Mumbai Zaveri Bazar reference rate, with 999 silver at Rs 1,92,075 per kg.
  • Both metals eased on the day — gold 999 fell Rs 461 per 10 grams and silver 999 fell Rs 2,798 per kg against the previous close.
  • Dhanteras is on Friday, November 6 and Diwali on Sunday, November 8, the peak buying days for coins, bars and 22K jewellery.
  • For buyers: the quoted rate excludes making charges, and a jewellery bill adds 3% GST on top — compare making charges across jewellers before paying.

Rates on October 30

Gold and silver traded lower on October 30 as families began final purchases ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali. On All India Bullion's Zaveri Bazar, Mumbai reference rate at 10:14 IST, 24K gold was Rs 14,387 per gram, or Rs 1,43,873 per 10 grams, 22K gold was Rs 13,179 per gram, and 999 silver was Rs 1,92,075 per kilogram.

City rates varied slightly around the Mumbai reference. Delhi was listed at Rs 1,44,073 per 10 grams for 24K and Rs 1,31,971 for 22K, Chennai at Rs 1,44,156 and Rs 1,32,047, Bengaluru at Rs 1,44,063 and Rs 1,31,962, and Kolkata at Rs 1,43,671 and Rs 1,31,602, with silver near Rs 1.92 lakh per kilogram in each city.

How October moved

The October 30 levels sit well below the month's highs. According to InvestingCube's review of the month, 24-carat gold opened October at Rs 1,47,904 per 10 grams, reached Rs 1,51,507, and fell to Rs 1,42,044 by October 23, a drop of roughly 3% from the start of the month and about 5% from the peak. Silver began October near Rs 2.26 lakh per kilogram, peaked at Rs 2.28 lakh on October 5, and fell to about Rs 1.94 lakh, a decline of roughly 14%.

That review attributed the correction mainly to global factors — a stronger dollar, higher US Treasury yields and the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metal — rather than weak Indian demand. Spot gold traded at or below $4,010 an ounce at points in the month, and silver dipped below $54 an ounce.

What Dhanteras buyers face

Dhanteras, on November 6, and Diwali, on November 8, are traditionally the heaviest physical buying days of the year for coins, bars and 22-carat jewellery. The October pullback gives buyers some relief after earlier surges, and the World Gold Council reported early signs of stronger seasonal demand, with manufacturers taking more orders and retailers restocking, according to InvestingCube.

High absolute prices still shape behaviour. Buyers often shift to smaller coins, lighter jewellery or lower weights rather than skipping a purchase entirely. Last year, record prices were estimated to have cut Dhanteras sales volumes by about 15% even as the value of sales rose.

What to check before you buy

The headline rate is not the final bill. Retail reference rates are quoted before making charges, and GST is added on a jewellery purchase. Check the hallmark and the six-character HUID code on hallmarked gold, verify it in the BIS CARE app, and ask for the making charge to be stated separately from the metal value. For diaspora families buying in India during a festival trip, or sending money home for a Dhanteras purchase, the same check applies: confirm the day's per-gram rate for the exact purity — 24K at 999 fineness for coins and bars, 22K at 916 for most jewellery — before agreeing a total.

Prices will continue to move with global yields, the dollar and central bank signals through the festival week. Spreading a larger purchase across two days, and comparing making charges between jewellers, remains the practical way to reduce the cost above the metal rate.
